Description: IAM role for payment orchestrator AI agent deployed via AWS AgentCore. Uses temporary credentials with session tags for fine-grained audit trail and access control.

TrustPolicy.Comment: Only AgentCore's service principal can assume this role, verified by a secret external ID to prevent confused deputy attacks.

Statement.Comment: Allow read-only access to customer accounts table, but ONLY for the payment orchestrator agent. Session tag condition prevents other agents (e.g., fraud-checker) from accessing this resource even if they use the same role.

Allow the agent to invoke the payment initiation API endpoint through API Gateway. Session tag condition ensures only the orchestrator agent (agentId=payment-orchestrator) can call this high-privilege endpoint.
Allow the agent to write audit logs to CloudWatch. Session tag ensures logs are tagged with this agent's identity.
Explicit deny for any agent with a different agentId. This is a defense-in-depth measure. If somehow another agent type uses this role (which should not happen), they are explicitly denied.
Enforce that every credential must include a userId tag. This requirement is typically enforced by a Service Control Policy (SCP) at the org level, but we include it here as defense-in-depth.
Enforce that every credential must include a sessionId tag for audit trail correlation. Enables tracing each API call back to the AgentCore session.

SessionTagPolicy.Comment: This policy would be enforced by AWS Organizations Service Control Policy (SCP) to mandate that all agent role assumptions include required tags.

CloudTrailExample.Comment: When this role is used to make an API call, CloudTrail records include session tag metadata

CredentialVendingCycle: 2. AgentCore calls sts:AssumeRole with PaymentOrchestratorAgentRole + session tags
3. AWS STS validates trust policy (only AgentCore allowed via external ID)
4. STS validates session tags meet policy requirements (agentId, userId, sessionId present)
5. STS vends temporary credentials with 15-minute TTL
7. Agent uses credentials to sign all requests (SigV4)
8. Every request includes session tags in CloudTrail (enables audit trail)
9. After 15 minutes, credentials expire → agent requests new credentials
10. No static keys ever stored or transmitted
RecommendedChanges: Replace <PLACEHOLDER> account IDs with your AWS account ID (e.g., 123456789012)
Replace <PLACEHOLDER> region with your region (e.g., us-east-1)
Replace <PLACEHOLDER> agentcore-account-id with the AWS account where AgentCore is deployed
Replace <PLACEHOLDER> agentcore-external-id-value with a random, confidential external ID (recommend: UUIDv4)
Replace <PLACEHOLDER: api-id> with your actual API Gateway API ID
Create similar roles for other agent types (fraud-detector, risk-scorer, etc.) with different agentId tag values
Enforce session tag requirements via Organization SCP (separate from this role)
AuditComplianceChecks: ✅ Every API call is traceable to: which user (userId tag) → which agent (agentId tag) → which session (sessionId tag)
✅ No shared service accounts — each agent type has dedicated role
✅ Per-agent revocation is possible — disable AgentCore's assumption of this role if agent is compromised
✅ Per-session audit correlation — use sessionId to link CloudTrail entries to agent session logs
✅ Compliant with banking audit requirements for authorization traceability
